Akbar studies the Euclidean Dirichlet problem for positive-definite biaxial Bianchi-IX Einstein metrics with negative cosmological constant and SU(2)×U(1)-invariant S^3 boundaries. Smoothness at a bolt ρ=ρb requires [d/dρ(Δ/(ρ²−L²))]ρb=1/(2kL). Writing Λ=−λ<0, the condition becomes 2Lλ(ρb²−L²)−(ρb−2L)=0, yielding two bolt radii ρb=[1±√(1+16λ²L⁴−16λL²)]/(4λL), allowed when λL²≤(2−√3)/4. Substitution gives two corresponding M(L) branches.       "title": "Einstein metrics and complex singularities",
      "representation": "David M. J. Calderbank and Michael A. Singer, “Einstein Metrics and Complex Singularities.” The paper studies special metrics on noncompact four-manifolds obtained as resolutions of isolated cyclic quotient singularities. It proves that toric resolutions admit finite-dimensional families of ALE scalar-flat Kähler metrics and, under c1(X)<0, complete non-Kähler self-dual Einstein metrics of negative scalar curvature. These metrics are toric and essentially explicit. The construction relies on the local classification of toric self-dual Einstein metrics by Calderbank–Pedersen: after choosing a hyperbolic-plane base and two commuting Killing fields, the metric is determined by an eigenfunction F satisfying Delta F = (3/4)F, with the Einstein metric expressed algebraically in F and its derivatives. Boundary zeros of F produce conformal infinity; suitable piecewise-linear or distributional boundary data yield smooth toric fillings and infinite-dimensional families of conformal structures on the boundary. Theorem B gives negative-scalar-curvature self-dual Einstein fillings of lens spaces for toric resolutions with c1(X)<0, while Theorem C gives infinitely many boundary conformal structures bounding such metrics. The paper also analyzes smooth extension over special orbits and proves a converse restriction: a special-orbit sphere in a toric negative-scalar-curvature self-dual Einstein metric must have self-intersection at least 3. The setting is noncompact and conformally compact/ALE, with self-duality and toric symmetry imposed; it does not address the general closed-manifold Einstein-existence statement in Yau Problem 26.",

      "title": "Seiberg-Witten Equations and Einstein Metrics on Finite Volume 4-Manifolds with Asymptotically Hyperbolic Ends",
      "representation": "Alex Xu studies Einstein metrics on noncompact oriented 4-manifolds of finite topological type with ends modeled on T^3×[0,∞). An asymptotically hyperbolic cusp is defined by comparison with dt^2+e^{-2t}g_{T^3}, where g_{T^3} is flat. The introduction cites finite-volume hyperbolic 4-manifolds as basic complete Einstein examples and describes Anderson's generalized Dehn filling theorem: starting from a finite-volume hyperbolic 4-manifold with T^3 cusps, filling selected cusps by D^2×T^2 along sufficiently long geodesics yields an Einstein metric, while unfilled ends remain asymptotically hyperbolic cusps. The paper states that these examples have signature zero and notes that existence with only T^3 cusps and nonzero signature was unknown to the author. It states a Dai–Wei inequality for complete asymptotically hyperbolic Einstein 4-manifolds, 2χ(X)≥3|σ(X)|. Its main results construct broad classes of 4-manifolds obtained by deleting embedded self-intersection-zero 2-tori that satisfy this inequality, yet admit no asymptotically hyperbolic Einstein metric. The obstruction combines scalar-curvature estimates, L² Seiberg–Witten theory, Biquard-style metric compactifications, and Pin^−(2) monopole invariants. The paper gives explicit warped metrics used in compactification: dt²+ψ_j²g_{T²}+φ_j²g_{S¹}, with the S¹ factor smoothly pinched off so the metric extends over D²×T²; these are auxiliary approximating metrics rather than claimed Einstein wormholes.       "representation": "Open-access research article by Javier Peraza and Martín Reiris, published in Classical and Quantum Gravity, volume 42, issue 8, article 085008, on 9 April 2025, DOI 10.1088/1361-6382/adc360. It studies static Myers/Korotkin–Nicolai vacuum 3+1 black holes and proves that certain members cannot be continuously deformed into axisymmetric stationary black holes with nonzero angular momentum. The solutions arise from periodic arrays first found by Myers in 1987 and rediscovered by Korotkin and Nicolai in 1994. In Weyl–Papapetrou coordinates, the lapse-related potential satisfies a linear equation; a periodic solution is formed by summing translated Schwarzschild potentials with a counterterm, while the remaining metric function is obtained by quadrature. Its integration constant is selected so that no struts occur between neighboring horizons. The universal solutions consist of infinitely many periodically aligned horizon segments, are regular outside the horizons, and are asymptotically Kasner rather than asymptotically flat. Quotienting by the axial-period translation yields a one-horizon spacetime with spatial topology an open solid torus minus an open 3-ball, complete at infinity. The article proves non-rotation results using reduced elliptic equations, Bakry–Émery curvature, geometric estimates, maximum-principle arguments, Komar angular momentum, and a Smarr-type identity.       "title": "ENTROPIES, VOLUMES, AND EINSTEIN METRICS",
      "representation": "Survey article by D. Kotschick on asymptotic invariants of closed smooth manifolds, including simplicial volume, spherical volume, volume entropy, topological entropy, minimal volume, spectral and isoperimetric invariants, and applications to Einstein 4-manifolds. It records the inequality chain relating these invariants and discusses homotopy or homological invariance of several of them. The central geometric result is Theorem 1: every closed oriented Einstein 4-manifold X satisfies χ(X) ≥ (3/2)|σ(X)| + λ(X)^4/(108π²), where λ(X) is minimal volume entropy. Equality is characterized by the assertion that every Einstein metric on X is flat, non-flat locally Calabi–Yau, or of constant negative sectional curvature. The proof uses Gauss–Bonnet and the signature formula, separates positive, zero, and negative scalar curvature, normalizes a negative Einstein metric by Ric_g=−g/3, applies Bishop entropy bounds, and invokes Ledrappier–Wang rigidity in the entropy-equality case. Corollaries give analogous bounds using spherical volume, minimal eigenvalue, isoperimetric constants, and simplicial volume. A further corollary treats nonzero-degree maps from Einstein 4-manifolds to real or complex hyperbolic manifolds: for a map of degree d to a real hyperbolic target Y, χ(X) ≥ (3/2)|σ(X)|+|d|χ(Y), with equality only if X is also real hyperbolic; the complex-hyperbolic analogue is strict. The paper also discusses smooth-structure dependence of minimal volume and constructs homeomorphic 4-manifolds with different collapsing behavior using Seiberg–Witten and monopole-class arguments.       "title": "The Cheeger Constant of an Asymptotically Locally Hyperbolic Manifold and the Yamabe Type of Its Conformal Infinity",
      "representation": "This paper studies asymptotically locally hyperbolic (ALH) manifolds, which are conformally compact Riemannian manifolds whose sectional curvatures approach -1 at infinity, and relates their Cheeger isoperimetric constant to the Yamabe type of their conformal infinity. The central question addressed is a sharpening of a result by J. Lee, who showed that non-negative Yamabe invariant of the boundary implies the bottom of the L2 spectrum of the Laplacian equals n²/4, but noted the converse fails. The authors answer Lee's question by proving that the Cheeger constant Ch(M,g) equals n if and only if the Yamabe invariant of the conformal infinity is non-negative, under curvature assumptions Ric_g + n g ≥ 0 and R_g + n(n+1) = o(r²). The paper first establishes that Ch(M,g) ≤ n for all ALH manifolds, and that strict inequality holds when a boundary component has negative Yamabe invariant and scalar curvature decays sufficiently. The main theorem's proof uses a positive function u satisfying Δu = (n+1)u with u ~ 1/r, whose logarithm f satisfies |∇f|² ≤ 1 and Δf ≥ n when the boundary Yamabe invariant is non-negative; integrating these inequalities over compact domains yields the isoperimetric inequality A(∂Ω) ≥ n V(Ω). The paper also proves connectedness of the conformal boundary under non-negative Yamabe invariant, using a Kasue comparison theorem. Consequences include the absence of smooth minimizers for the Cheeger constant, a characterization of hyperbolic quotients satisfying the linear isoperimetric inequality in terms of the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set, and an extension of Lee's spectral result to the principal eigenvalue of the p-Laplacian, showing λ_{1,p}(M) = (n/p)^p when the boundary Yamabe invariant is non-negative.       "representation": "Michael T. Anderson’s 2005 paper surveys the moduli space and degeneration theory of conformally compact Einstein (Poincare-Einstein/AH) metrics. It defines the boundary map from Einstein metrics to conformal infinity and states that this map is Fredholm of index zero. It reviews asymptotic expansions at conformal infinity, local stability, unique continuation, and boundary control. For globally defined four-dimensional settings with controlled boundary data, it presents a trichotomy for sequences: (I) smooth convergence to a Poincare-Einstein metric; (II) convergence to an orbifold-singular Einstein metric with finitely many cone-type singularities; or (III) convergence to a cusp Einstein metric on a connected manifold, possibly with orbifold points. In the cusp case, the limit retains the conformal boundary and acquires complete finite-volume ends; base points near the conformal boundary yield pointed Gromov-Hausdorff convergence, smooth away from singularities, while other base points may see additional finite-volume limits.
